# Handoff: Docs Site Final Polish

## What this is

A handoff for the next session to cross-reference the docs site against the actual project codebase and bring every page to a finished, marker-ready state. The docs site was drafted while the project was still being built — every page needs to be updated to reflect what's actually built and deployed *now*.

## What's already done (this session)

- **Methodology updated** — replaced "Sprint review" with "Sprint reflection (Sprint Log)", switched to dynamic/initiative-based task selection (no pre-assignment), retained product backlog. Committed `01ba7dc`.
- **Sprint Log added** — `docs/sprint-log.md` with full Sprint 1 week-by-week task tables. Added to nav under Process > Sprint Log.
- **Full audit completed** — every doc page read and issues catalogued below.

## Setup for this work

The docs repo and the project code repo should be in a shared parent folder so the agent can cross-reference:

```
<parent-folder>\
├── sportsanalytics\                      ← actual project code (Gitea repo)
└── Innovation-Documentation-Website\     ← this docs site
```

The agent needs to read the project's actual source code (controllers, schema, routes, tests, deploy configs) to verify what the docs claim vs. what's actually built.

---

## Audit: Every doc that needs updating

### 1. `docs/index.md`
- **Issue:** Says "This site is under active construction (Sprint 1)"
- **Fix:** Rewrite the Status section to reflect the project's current state. Remove "under construction" language.

### 2. `docs/requirements.md`
- **Issue:** Full of `TBD` owners and issue columns. Says "not yet in the pipeline" for axe-core. References "no deploy target" for CI/CD.
- **Fix:** Fill in actual owners from the sprint log. Update CI/CD row to reflect that deploy is now set up (Cloudflare Pages + Render per ADR-003). Update the axe-core note. Remove the "TBD owners/issues are placeholders" note at the bottom.

### 3. `docs/design/architecture.md`
- **Issue:** "Open questions" section references things now resolved:
  - `nba_api` integration path — ingestion service is now built (see sprint log: Josh's ingestion work, Daniel's coverage/search work)
  - "Production hosting — not decided" — ADR-003 is decided and implemented (Cloudflare + Render + Supabase)
  - "Whether any endpoint is auth-gated" — Daniel added authenticated route protection (PR #44, sprint log week of 18 Aug)
- **Prediction section:** Says "not yet built" — predictions ARE built (Josh: GamePrediction model, predictor service, predictions page, court view)
- **Fix:** Rewrite open questions to reflect resolved state. Update the architecture diagram to include ingestion service, prediction pipeline, and deployment topology. Update the prediction/optimisation diagram.

### 4. `docs/tech-stack.md`
- **Issue:** Three "Open question" admonitions:
  - "Prisma vs. Drizzle" — Prisma is confirmed, not an open question
  - "`nba_api` is Python, API is TypeScript" — ingestion service is now built, this is resolved
  - "Not yet decided: Production hosting" — ADR-003 is decided
- **Jobs/queue section:** Lists Redis, BullMQ, Zod, S3 as "Decided, not yet implemented" — verify against actual project if these are still planned or dropped
- **Vitest row:** Says "no test files exist yet" — tests DO exist now (Owen wrote them, sprint log week of 4 Aug)
- **CI/CD host confirmed note:** Says "CI only, no CD" — CD is now set up (Cloudflare Pages auto-deploy, Render auto-deploy via GitHub mirror)
- **Fix:** Remove resolved open-question admonitions. Update Vitest row. Update CI/CD note to reflect CD is live. Verify Redis/BullMQ/Zod/S3 status against actual project.

### 5. `docs/design/feature-tiers.md`
- **Issue:** "What's still a proposal, not a decision" warning — predictions are now built
- **"Still open" section:** Model choices, feature set, recommendation layer scope — verify what's actually been decided/built
- **Basic tier:** Says "Prediction (new, not yet built)" — team-level prediction IS built (Josh: Elo win probability, Four Factors margin)
- **Fix:** Remove the "proposal" warning. Update Basic tier to reflect what's built. Update "Still open" to reflect current state.

### 6. `docs/design/roadmap.md`
- **Issue:** "Draft, not assigned" warning — work has been assigned and completed
- **Sprint 1 section:** Says "Remaining: nba_api ingestion path" — ingestion is now built
- **"Still open" section:** Individual ownership, advanced tier scope — verify current state
- **Fix:** Remove "Draft" warning. Update Sprint 1 status to reflect what was completed. Update Sprint 2/3/Submission sections with what's actually done vs. remaining.

### 7. `docs/design/api-design.md`
- **Issue:** Only lists 5 original endpoints (players CRUD, teams CRUD, player stats). Missing many confirmed endpoints:
  - `GET /v1/games` (Owen, week of 13 Aug)
  - `GET /v1/games/:id/prediction` (Josh, week of 18 Aug)
  - Prediction/optimizer endpoints (Josh, Owen)
  - Search endpoints (Daniel: player and team search, PR #42)
  - Auth endpoints (BetterAuth mounts at `/api/auth/*`)
  - Ingestion endpoints (Josh: ingestion orchestrator, PR #34)
- **"Not yet confirmed" section:** Auth endpoints, prediction endpoints — now built
- **Fix:** Rebuild the endpoint table from actual `apps/api/src/**/*.controller.ts` files. Remove outdated "not confirmed" caveats. Update response shapes if new ones exist.

### 8. `docs/design/wireframes.md` (UI Overview)
- **Issue:** "What's not built yet" section says:
  - "Teams list/profile pages" — Teams pages ARE built (Owen: Teams pages with TanStack Query, shadcn/ui, sprint log week of 4 Aug)
  - "Auth screens" — verify current state
  - "Any optimisation/analytics UI" — predictions page, court view, optimizer are built
- **Navigation:** Says "Sidebar with three links" — nav has changed (top navbar replaced sidebar, Owen week of 13 Aug)
- **Fix:** Rewrite to reflect all current screens. Update navigation description. Add new screens (Games, Predictions, Teams, Search, etc.).

### 9. `docs/design/erd.md`
- **Issue:** "One caveat on freshness" warning — schema has likely grown since initial snapshot
- **"Still open" section:** Says "nothing in the schema touches optimisation" — verify if prediction/optimization tables were added
- **Missing entities:** Verify if new tables were added for: predictions, ingestion data, optimizer
- **Fix:** Re-read `apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma` and rebuild the entities list from the actual current schema. Remove outdated freshness warning.

### 10. `docs/getting-started.md`
- **Issue:** "Placeholder values" warning at top — should be replaced with real values from actual `.env.example` files
- **"No test files exist yet" note** — tests exist now
- **Fix:** Remove placeholder warning (verify env vars against actual `.env.example` files). Remove "no test files" note. Verify all commands still work against current project structure.

### 11. `docs/security.md`
- **Issue:** "Open compliance question" about password reset — verify if this was resolved or is still open
- **"Not yet implemented" section:** Lists HTTPS/TLS, rate limiting, security headers, input validation — verify what's actually in place now (Render has managed TLS, Cloudflare has TLS, etc.)
- **Secret scanning:** Says "not yet in the pipeline" — verify current state
- **Fix:** Update each section against actual project state. Move items from "not yet implemented" to "implemented" where applicable. Keep genuinely open items clearly marked.

### 12. `docs/ci-cd.md`
- **Issue:** "No CD stages" / "no deploy target" language throughout — deploy IS set up now
- **Open items section:** Item 7 says "eventually CD once hosting is decided" — hosting is decided
- **Fix:** Add a CD section describing the actual deploy pipeline (Gitea → GitHub mirror → Cloudflare Pages auto-deploy for web, GitHub mirror → Render auto-deploy for API). Update open items.

### 13. `docs/decisions/adr-003-hosting-topology.md`
- **Issue:** Status says "Proposed — awaiting team review" — this has been implemented
- **Fix:** Change status to "Accepted" (or "Implemented"). Update any "not yet deployed" language.

### 14. `docs/meetings/client/index.md`
- **Issue:** Multiple action items with "TBD" due dates (2026-08-21 meeting actions)
- **Fix:** Fill in actual due dates where known, or mark as "Sprint 2" / "Sprint 3" where appropriate. The 2026-08-13 meeting also has TBD dates.

### 15. `docs/meetings/client/index.md` line 167
- **Issue:** `####note` should be `???note` (broken admonition syntax — missing the `?`)
- **Fix:** Change `####note` to `??? note`

---

## Missing AI Usage Ledger entries

The ledger (`docs/ai-usage.md`) is missing rows for these transcripts that exist in `docs/transcripts/ai_transcripts/`:

| Transcript file | What it covers (add ledger row) |
|---|---|
| `2026-08-15-Owen-Claude-API-FrontEnd.txt` | Owen's API + frontend work |
| `2026-08-21-adrian-qoder-fix-broken-links.jsonl` | Fixing MkDocs broken links |
| `2026-08-23-adrian-qoder-client-meeting-docs.jsonl` | Documenting client meeting notes |
| Any new transcripts from the project repo | Scan for additional transcripts (Daniel's, Owen's, etc.) |

Also check for "Not yet provided" in the Transcript column and fill in links where transcripts now exist.

---

## General principles for the polish pass

1. **Read the actual code** — don't guess. Check controllers for endpoints, `schema.prisma` for entities, `.env.example` for env vars, workflow files for CI/CD state.
2. **Remove all "not yet" / "TBD" / "placeholder" / "draft" / "open question" language** — replace with facts from the codebase. If something is genuinely still open, say so clearly but don't leave stale warnings about things that are now resolved.
3. **Write in past tense for what's built** — the docs should read as a record of a completed project, not a planning document.
4. **Keep the AI declaration** at the bottom of each file.
5. **Rebuild the site** (`mkdocs build --strict`) after all changes to verify no broken links.
6. **Commit with a clear message** when done.

University of the WitwatersrandOverviewCOMS3011A Project Brief
1Overview
1.1Projects & Groups
Each project is broken down into three tiers: Basic, Intermediate, Advanced. To achieve the basic tier, 
your project needs to meet all the listed key and basic requirements, as well as achieve the standard of a 
minimum viable product. The intermediate tier needs to meet all the listed basic requirements and the 
intermediate requirements. The expected standard is that of a functional and useful product. The 
advanced tier needs to meet all listed requirements, even those potentially introduced part way through 
the semester. The standard of an advanced project is one that can be released to market the day of 
submission.
You can find a brief problem statement for each project in this document, but additional information will 
be provided through project specific briefs.
Groups are 4 - 6 members. Please select your group carefully as you may not change your group once 
the semester has started.
Your group will be assigned a tutor as a ‘client’. Their role is to help guide you on the development 
process and make decisions around if a feature is ‘complete’ or not. Your tutor will act as the first point 
of contact for any questions about your project, but the lecturer will be available if you would like 
further clarification. You will not be marked by your client, but by other tutors. The client is however 
expected to provide some context to the marking tutor on your interactions with them.
1.2Milestones & Reports
1.2.1Milestone 1: Sprint 1
Milestone 1 is aimed at project setup and the basics of a project. Setting up the project repositories, 
getting the largest ‘blockers’ out of the way, making sure you and your group have a strong direction for 
the rest of the semester.
1.2.2Milestone 2: Sprint 2
Milestone 2 is the midpoint of the project, where by the end of this sprint you have a strong base for the 
project. The most important features are implemented, even if there are issues, and the project is 
moving towards a stable product through testing and reviews.
1.2.3Milestone 3: Sprint 3
Milestone 3 is aimed at getting the project into a near-complete state. Most features should be 
implemented, and mostly working. The project should have gone through reviews and you should be 
evaluating the state of the project from a qualitative perspective.
1.2.4Milestone 4: Submission
Milestone 4 is the final submission. Your project should work, work well, and do what it needs to.

University of the WitwatersrandOverviewCOMS3011A Project Brief
The marking of milestone 4 is evaluating your entire project holistically. Over the entire dev-cycle of the 
project, has your group been consistent with your methodology, how has your projects requirements 
and plans evolved.
1.2.5Report 1: Group Report
The group report is a summary of the project’s development and a reflection as a group of the entire 
project. What decisions were made through out the project, why did they occur and what can be done to 
improve upon them in the future.
The report should be presented as a technical document with references, an introduction, body, 
conclusion and appendices.
1.2.6Report 2: Individual Report
The individual report is a reflection of your growth and development throughout the project. What 
challenges did you encounter, what new technology did you learn about, how did you work as a team, 
and most importantly, something you are proud of.
The report is an opinionated piece, but should still be presented as academic writing. It should have an 
introduction, body, conclusion, appendices and use references and evidence based motivation.
1.2.7Report 3: Peer Review
The peer review is split into two sections:
1.An anonymous review of your group members
2.A personal evaluation of your performance
Your mark is calculated by taking your personal rating and the average rating of your group members.
The peer review will act as a multiplier of your group marks. If you achieve a peer review mark of 
greater or equal to 50%, you will receive all your group marks. If you achieve a mark less than 50%, you 
will receive a mark multiplied by a specified value for every group component of the project.
